test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Surbhi invested a total sum of Rs. 47,740 in three schemes A, B and C such that the simple interest received from scheme A at 10% p.a. after 3 years, from scheme B at 9% p.a. after 4 years and from scheme C at 8% p.a. after 5 years were the same. What is the positive difference (in Rs.) between the sums invested in schemes C and A?
solution:
**Given:**

Total sum = Rs. 47740

**Concept Used:**

SI = (P × R × T)/100

**Calculation:**

Let the amount in scheme A be x, in scheme B be y and then in scheme C is (47740 - x - y) 

According to the problem statement, Since the interest is same,

⇒ (x × 10 × 3 )/100 = (y × 9 × 4)/100 = {(47740 - x - y) × 8 × 5}/100

Using first two relations

⇒ 5x = 6y

⇒ y = 5x/6 ----(i)

Solving 1st and 3rd equation

⇒ 3x = 190960 – 4x – 4y

Using (i)

⇒ 3x = 190960 - 4x - 4(5x/6)

⇒ x = 18480

⇒ y = 5x/6 = 15400

⇒ In scheme C = 47740 - x - y = 13860

Difference (in Rs.) between the sums invested in schemes C and A = 18480 - 13860 = Rs. 4620

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**
